sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Delaware?
sections.html:
Delaware property tax is billed locally, by county tax offices, and the rate you pay depends mostly on your school district. Kent County's assessment office says the tax is the taxable value multiplied by the rate, with the school district setting most of that rate and the county government and county library adding to it.

That means two houses with the same value can get different bills, even inside one county. A home in the Colonial school district in New Castle County is billed on different rates than one in Appoquinimink. When you plan a sale, read the bill for your own parcel and the district printed on it, not a neighbor's number.

Delaware has only three counties, so the structure is simple to keep in your head.

  • New Castle County: the northern county, with five school districts that lie entirely within it plus a vocational-technical district.
  • Kent County: the middle county, billed by the Kent County Receiver of Taxes.
  • Sussex County: the southern county, billed through the Sussex County Treasury and Billing offices in Georgetown.

sections.h2: Why did Delaware reassess every property recently?
sections.html:
Delaware reassessed because a court ordered it after decades without new values. Spotlight Delaware reports that New Castle and Kent counties had not reassessed since the 1980s and Sussex had not done so since 1974, and that a 2020 Court of Chancery ruling followed a 2018 lawsuit over the old system.

The same reporting says House Bill 62 now requires each county to reassess every five years. Kent County's current values are as of July 1, 2023, according to the county's assessment FAQ. New Castle County's values are as of July 1, 2024.

For a seller, the reassessment matters in two ways. First, your assessed value now tracks market value much more closely than it did, so a buyer or a cash investor reading your bill will see a number tied to a recent date. Second, Spotlight Delaware notes that roughly a third of owners saw lower taxes, a third higher and a third about the same, and that exemptions and abatements were not built into the new assessed values. They are applied once a rate is set.

Kent County's FAQ adds that a sale does not trigger a reassessment.

sections.h2: When are Delaware property taxes due?
sections.html:
In Kent and Sussex counties the annual bill is due September 30. New Castle County's tax code sets a July 1 due date with a penalty that starts after September 1, so New Castle owners should read their own bill for the exact deadline.

CountyTax yearBills mailedDueLate cost
KentJune 1 to May 31Typically by mid-August, after school districts set ratesSeptember 30Ask the Kent Tax Office
SussexJuly 1 to June 30Early AugustSeptember 30 (supplemental bills Dec. 31, Mar. 31, June 30)1.5% per month
New CastleSet by 9 Del. C. ch. 86Statement within 30 days after the due dateJuly 1 under 9 Del. C. 86016% after September 1, then 1% each month

Sussex County adds that a missing bill does not cancel a penalty. Its tax office says the owner is responsible for paying on time even if the bill never arrived. New Castle's code says the same thing: not receiving a statement does not excuse timely payment.

New Castle's code also requires the Office of Finance to send at least one written demand for unpaid taxes by December 15 each year. A residential owner with a primary residence and a bill at least $300 above the prior year can qualify for a payment plan of at least three equal school-tax installments. Those plan provisions are written to expire on August 12, 2028.

sections.h2: What are the school tax rates in New Castle County?
sections.html:
New Castle County school districts split their rates in 2025, charging homes a lower rate than apartments, commercial and industrial property. Spotlight Delaware published the new per-$100 rates after the school boards voted in August 2025.

To estimate a school bill, divide the assessment by 100 and multiply by the residential rate for the district. The same source says the county aimed to mail recalculated bills by September 30, 2025, with a November 30 payment date, and that overpayments of more than $50 could be refunded or credited.

Rates change every year, so treat this as a snapshot of how the split works rather than a quote for the current bill.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and credits can lower a Delaware tax bill?
sections.html:
Delaware offers a school tax credit for seniors, a county exemption for low-income seniors and the disabled, and full exemptions for government, school, religious and some charitable property. Most of them require an application, and most have a spring deadline.

  • Senior School Property Tax Credit: the state Department of Finance says the owner must be 65 or older and the property must be the primary residence. Applications are due April 30. Residency rules depend on when you became a Delaware domiciliary: before 2013, no waiting period beyond eligibility in the following tax year; from 2013 through 2017, three consecutive years; from January 1, 2018, ten consecutive years. The bill must be paid in full by the end of the tax year. The state's page shows two different maximum amounts, so confirm the current cap with your county before you rely on a figure.
  • Kent County senior and disability exemption: age 65 by May 31 or total disability, income limits of $18,000 for one applicant or $24,750 combined with a spouse, and yearly reapplication by April 30. Title must be in the applicant's name.
  • General exemptions: government property, school property used for education, religious property not held as an investment, certain charitable property and parkland owned by civic groups such as homeowners' associations.

Sussex County sends applications for its senior, disability and State 65 exemptions through the Billing Office at (302) 855-7871.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Delaware property assessment?
sections.html:
You appeal in writing to your county, and deadlines are firm. In Kent County an annual appeal must reach the Assessment Office by 5:00 p.m. on January 31 to affect the tax year beginning June 1, and a postmark is not accepted. Appeals of quarterly supplemental increases must be filed within 30 days of notice. The county notes that deadlines can change in reassessment years.

During the reassessment, Spotlight Delaware described a two-step path: an informal review with the contractor, Tyler Technologies, and then an appeal through the county. For New Castle County, the official summary at the top of this page gives the Board of Assessment Review deadline of March 15.

The refund rules deserve attention before a sale. Kent County says its refund policy follows state law and covers limited cases, such as tax paid while an appeal is pending or a duplicate bill. An error found after the appeal window usually does not produce a refund. Delaware law, in the county's words, puts the burden of making sure assessment data is accurate on the property owner.

If you plan to sell, an appeal that is still open at closing is a loose end. Tell the title company about it so the proceeds and any refund are handled in writing.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Delaware house with property tax due?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax in Delaware is collected out of the sale or, if it goes unpaid long enough, through a court-supervised tax sale. The seller should expect the title company to find the balance and pay it from proceeds at closing.

Under the monition method in the Delaware Code, the tax collector files in Superior Court, the sheriff posts a notice on the property, and the notice gives 20 days to pay before the tax authority can ask for a sale. After a tax sale the owner has 60 days after court approval to redeem by paying the purchaser the price plus 15 percent and costs. Kent County's sheriff procedures also describe tax sales held about every three months, with the full bid due the same day.

Practical steps for an owner with a bill outstanding:

  • Pull the current bill and any supplemental bills from the county tax portal.
  • Check whether a mortgage escrow already paid it. Sussex County offers an EscrowCheck tool and forwards bills to mortgage companies.
  • After closing, report the ownership change to the county assessment office. Sussex lists (302) 855-7824 for ownership changes.
  • Keep proof of payment for any exemption you are leaving behind.

A cash buyer who purchases a house as-is can close with the tax balance paid from proceeds, which is often the simplest route when back taxes are growing by the month. Cash Home Buyers can talk through your balance, but any figure depends on the county records for your parcel.

faqs.q: Does Delaware have a state property tax?
faqs.a: The sources used for this guide describe property tax as billed by counties and school districts, and none of them describes a state-level levy. Your bill comes from the county tax office and reflects your school district's rate.

faqs.q: When is the Delaware property tax due date?
faqs.a: Kent and Sussex counties list September 30 for the annual bill. New Castle County's code sets July 1 with penalties after September 1, so check the due date printed on your New Castle bill.

faqs.q: Will selling my house trigger a new assessment?
faqs.a: Not in Kent County. Its assessment office says a sale does not trigger reassessment, and values change only for a countywide reassessment, a change to the property or a corrected error. Delaware counties now reassess every five years.

faqs.q: Can seniors reduce Delaware property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The state Senior School Property Tax Credit covers homeowners 65 and older on their primary residence, with an April 30 application deadline. Kent County also has an income-limited senior and disability exemption. Confirm the current credit amount with your county.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay my Delaware property tax?
faqs.a: Penalties start, such as 1.5% per month in Sussex County and 6% after September 1 plus 1% a month in New Castle County. Continued non-payment can lead to a monition tax sale, where the owner has 60 days after court approval to redeem by paying the buyer the price plus 15 percent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Delaware house to a cash buyer if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. The tax balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company confirms the payoff with the county. The earlier you sell, the less penalty builds up.
